To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

The superconducting granule colloid is a model for a granular superconductor, and the avalanche behaviour of this system at very low temperature is an example of the behaviour of a granular superconducting material at the transition temperature.

(a) The critical current density of aluminium and zinc granular superconductors is enhanced at very low temperatures (b) The superconducting transition is shifted to higher temperatures in granular aluminium and zinc (c) A new superconducting state is observed for granular aluminium and possibly zinc at very low temperature, characterized by an enhancement of the critical current density and a shift of the superconducting transition to higher temperatures.

we have observed the following effects in granules of aluminium and zinc: (a) a large increase in the critical current density with decreasing temperature; (b) a large increase of the critical current density in a magnetic field of about 0.1 Tesla; (c) a large increase (by a factor of about ten) of the critical current in a magnetic field with increasing temperature; (d) a large increase with decreasing temperature of the current at the onset of the transition to the normal state
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of superconducting granular systems at very low temperature (below 1 K) and in the presence of a strong external magnetic field.

the study of the magnetic behaviour of superconducting granular systems at very low temperature, with the purpose of understanding the mechanisms responsible for the superconducting properties of these materials.
a new class of materials: granular superconductors.

, in the case of aluminium granules, the critical temperature is not a constant, but depends on the magnetic field and on the temperature itself.
, for a given sample, the critical temperature is not a constant, but it depends on the temperature history of the sample.

we have found that the critical field for a granule is much larger than that of a bulk sample of the same material, and that the granules exhibit a large critical current, which is much larger than the critical field.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the superconducting granular system is a good candidate for the study of non-equilibrium phenomena in superconductors.

we have demonstrated that the granules are not only sensitive to temperature, but also to the magnetic field, and the magnetic field can induce superconductivity in the granules, which can lead to a large change in the granules’ magnetic field.
we have shown that the avalanche phenomenon is not limited to granular materials.
